one_star_reviews.text:
I've lived in Parque Alcosa for many years, and both my mother and I have our primary care physician here. Since the recent changes in doctors, the care has been very disappointing.

My mother had a telephone appointment to renew her sick leave certificate and also to update her medication. However, she was assigned a different doctor, and apparently, he never made the call, didn't update her medication, and didn't process the sick leave certificate. What's most concerning is that he was later recorded as having done his job correctly, even though we have evidence that this wasn't the case.

My mother had to wait to get a new in-person appointment to personally resolve a situation that should have been handled during the initial consultation. I believe this demonstrates a lack of professionalism, responsibility, and empathy towards the patient.

It's outrageous that we have to resort to this in a health center and that a patient can't trust that their medical needs will be properly addressed. If a professional is assigned to care for another doctor's patients, they must assume that responsibility with the same seriousness and professional ethics.

This isn't about judging anyone based on their background, but about demanding that all healthcare professionals, regardless of who they are or where they come from, properly fulfill their obligations and treat patients with respect, responsibility, and empathy.

I hope this incident is reviewed and that situations like this never happen again.

They NEVER answer the phone during their opening hours. If you call Salud Responde to make an appointment, they tell you that this clinic doesn't accept appointments through them. If you try to access your primary care physician's appointment through ClicSalud+, half the time it says the calendar isn't available and that you have to come in person. The worst health center in all of Andalusia. This is for you all.

Our experience at this clinic was terrible.

We took our dog to the clinic because he needed help, but they sent him back saying he was fine, even though he couldn't even stand up. A few hours later, he started bleeding profusely and we had to rush him back to the clinic.
The worst part was the treatment we received. We arrived with the dog in a very serious condition and he was admitted. That night they told us he was better, but the next day no one bothered to call us to inform us of the situation. I had to call myself, only to find out that our dog had died. Not a single call, no explanation, not a shred of empathy. They simply said, "Oh, the dog? That dog died during the night." We had never seen anything like it. The lack of professionalism and humanity was incredibly bad. The care received was completely incompetent.
Losing a dog is hard enough, but receiving this treatment is unforgivable. On top of all that, we paid a lot of money for a service that was far from what a veterinary clinic should offer.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our regular vet, Claudia, is an excellent professional. In fact, we left our previous vet when we met her.

But BEWARE that ÁLVARO DOES NOT treat you. He owns the clinic, and I believe he only sees patients occasionally.
Last month, we went with my dog, who was wearing his muzzle, and he growled at the assistant when she was about to draw blood. At that moment, Álvaro came in and, without warning or asking our consent, lifted the dog up, grabbing him with both hands by the front of his neck, leaving only his hind legs on the ground and the rest of his body suspended by his neck.
The maneuver was so abrupt and violent that when I asked him to let go of the dog, he ignored my request, and I had to remove his hands myself to get him to release him.
This is ethically unacceptable because he inflicted completely unnecessary physical and emotional suffering on the animal. Furthermore, interventions of this kind only produce fear and a loss of trust in the dog towards the people handling it, thus generating greater sensitivity towards future veterinary examinations, hindering clinical assessment, and increasing the risk of defensive responses. For this reason, modern veterinary medicine has handling and restraint protocols designed to minimize the animal's fear and stress.

It is also especially concerning when a veterinarian acts according to conceptions of canine behavior widely discredited by modern ethology and current veterinary management recommendations. These theories based on "dominance," according to which the animal must be subdued through physical force or induced into submission through fear or panic, are not only obsolete but also incompatible with current principles of animal welfare and the ethical practice of the veterinary profession.

We decided to file a complaint, even though he owns the clinic, and his behavior when we went to request a complaint form only reinforced our conviction that he is unfit to care for animals or to deal with the public in any way.
In short, for your dog's sake, avoid this professional at all costs if you go to the clinic.

At first, it seemed promising: a gym with classes, with basic but functional equipment… There were many problems, and it seemed like things were going to improve, but after the initial surge in memberships, people started leaving, and rightly so. Everything has gone downhill:
- There are no instructors, and when they are there, they're just running from one class to another like slaves. I understand why people want to leave.

- There's no reception desk, and there's almost always a sign hanging up.

- There's a QR code for suggestions, but they neither answer nor pay any attention to them.

- The bathrooms often don't have toilet paper, and there's no one checking. But of course, if you go to ask for it, since there's no one at reception…
- It's incredibly hot.

The management changed recently, but I think it's even worse since they took over. You're dying of heat, and I think it's hotter than the permitted temperature. Only if you go first thing in the morning can you manage to work out without being sweltering.

The only way to contact them is by email, but they take a while to respond.

one_star_reviews.text:
I thought the police force's main mission was to serve and protect; but from the moment I arrived early, I was greeted with laughter and comments among the staff about the frustration of serving one person after another, and then about the quality of the paper on my NIE (Foreigner Identification Number). Since I was missing a document, they told me I had to make another appointment, but because the documents were easy to obtain and it was still within my appointment time, I rushed over and returned sweating within my allotted time. However, they decided they would first attend to the people with appointments 20 minutes later and then to me. Five minutes later, though, they informed me they wouldn't do that, even though I arrived on time and the clerk had assured me I would be seen later.

In the end, they kicked me out of the station like a bouncer at a nightclub telling you you're not on the list, puffing out their chests and moving towards me to remove me.

This made me feel excluded, discriminated against, and belittled: as a woman, as a foreigner, and for being alone, especially when I saw that the woman (who spoke English, was seen before her scheduled appointment time, and was accompanied by a Spanish man) was waited on until she left to get something she needed, returned, and they finished before her appointment time.

If I could, I would rate it with less than 1 or 0 stars. Terrible service, because they have zero desire to work, poor customer service, and absolutely no empathy.

My experience with the food at this care home has not been good. I feel the portions served are insufficient, and sometimes too much water is added to the food to increase its volume, resulting in very little seasoning, bland flavor, and, in my opinion, nutritional value.

I am particularly concerned that some residents are losing weight and, according to what I've heard, feeling weak. I believe this should be taken very seriously, as nutrition is fundamental to maintaining the well-being and health of older adults.

Furthermore, when a resident cannot or does not want to eat the meal served, no alternative is offered, so they may end up eating very little or practically nothing.
I believe it is necessary to review both the quantity and the quality and nutritional value of the meals, as well as offer alternatives when a resident cannot eat the planned menu. People living in a care home should receive sufficient, varied, and appropriate nutrition.

one_star_reviews.text:
COMPLAINT

I wish to formally register my dissatisfaction with some situations that have been occurring at the store.

Last month, my daughter went shopping around 9:15 p.m., even though the store closes at 9:30 p.m. She was only going to buy eggs and tuna. However, she was denied entry, with the explanation that there were too many people in the checkout line. I understand that there may be a closing time, but I believe that, with 15 minutes still remaining before closing and for a purchase of only two items, the situation was quite unpleasant.

Furthermore, for several days now, I have noticed that at certain times the traditional loaf of bread is no longer available, leaving only other, more expensive options.

And today, specifically, my daughter went to buy bread at approximately 8:15 p.m. and was told that they would no longer be baking any more bread. I find this situation quite surprising, considering the store is open until 9:30 PM and there's still more than an hour until closing time.
I completely understand that certain products may run out, but when this happens frequently, especially with a basic item like bread, it's quite inconvenient for customers.
I hope this situation will be reviewed and that both product availability and customer service, as well as the policy regarding entry before closing time, will be improved.
I hope this complaint will help change the situation so we can continue shopping normally.
Thank you for your attention.

one_star_reviews.text:
This is the second review we are publishing, as the first one was deleted. We were also surprised to have been exposed on Instagram after expressing how we felt during our experience.

At no time was our intention to be disrespectful or hurt anyone. We simply explained our experience and how we felt. We left the consultation crying on more than one occasion because of the way we were spoken to, and we believe that, as clients, we have the right to express it.

During one of the visits we had, she told us that she could not speak because she had no voice and that, for this reason, they had to speak for her. We understood this perfectly and at no time did we reproach her for it. What surprised us was that later, on Instagram, she did speak perfectly in videos to advertise her clinic.

We would also have liked a little self-criticism and for her to be able to recognize that perhaps at some point she may have made a mistake. For us, making a video on Instagram to say that we are bad people is not the right way to handle a situation like this.

We have been to other clinics and, even if we may have different opinions or disagree on something, we have always been treated with education, respect and, above all, humanity.

And we want to make one thing very clear: this review is not about whether the treatment works better or worse, or whether the clinic is good or bad professionally. This is about HOW we felt, the treatment we received and, above all, a question of humanity and respect.

We have only explained our experience and will continue to do so with respect. We do not want to enter into any war or conflict, but we will not accept that in order to express how we felt, we are made to look like bad people on Instagram.

one_star_reviews.text:
I went hoping to resolve a tension headache, encouraged by the positive reviews, but despite attending a considerable number of sessions and strictly following the instructions for continued progress at home, there was no improvement whatsoever.

From the very beginning, deficiencies in the treatment were apparent. Being located near Paseo de la Castellana, there's a lot of traffic, and despite being on the ninth floor, on several occasions the noise of a car horn or a passing ambulance would be picked up and remain on the recording. Also, it seems he doesn't manage the timing well. Many times he either ran out of time or had too much time to finish the session, and he would make abrupt changes in the music, which at least I noticed in the recording. But something tells me that even without these and other deficiencies, I still wouldn't have had any luck.

I don't think he's a fraud. I don't think a scammer can stay active for so long, and I want to believe that all the reviews, or at least the vast majority of them, are genuine, but unfortunately, all this has only served to get me money, and that's what I have to tell you.

one_star_reviews.text:
From the beginning, I asked if the diagnostic tests were administered by psychologists and doctors, and they assured me they were. Later, I discovered this wasn't the case. Two days of tests, each lasting over two hours, were conducted by an extremely young person listed on the public registry of the Official College of Psychologists of Madrid with a degree but listed as NOT PRACTICING. They presented her as "clinical psychology" and listed her under the "Doctor" field in the WhatsApp messages where they scheduled my appointments.

Then, after much back and forth, during which they kept me waiting for days without giving me an answer, withholding my money, and offering no solution, they finally refunded my money (which wasn't the solution I wanted; I needed an urgent diagnosis and asked them to repeat the tests or proceed with a significant discount, given that the tests had been administered by someone listed as non-practicing and inexperienced). They then sent me an email denying all responsibility and arrogantly and brazenly claiming that they had done everything perfectly. And that's when they told me that this person could perform the tests because she was an intern. Something I was never informed about.

And that has its own regulations, although they seem to ignore them: Article 8.4 of Law 41/2002 states that the patient has the right to be informed when the diagnostic procedures applied to them are part of a teaching project, and that their prior written authorization is required. I wasn't informed of anything, nor was any authorization requested. She performed the tests on me alone, without anyone supervising her at any time.

So, run from this clinic. They're shameless; they use recent graduates as interns without informing the patient or asking for their consent—that is, without experience to perform tests of this magnitude, tests that can change your life. They're cheapskates and, on top of that, they act like they know everything.

If you still decide to try them because you can't find another clinic, ask for the professional registration number of all their staff (when I asked, they never gave it to me; I had to find it myself) and ask them to certify that they aren't interns, or at least inform you if they are so you can decide whether to accept. This is a right recognized in Article 5.1.e of Law 44/2003. For the money they charge, I would never have agreed to have the tests done by an intern, but maybe it's just me demanding quality when I spend my money.

And now, because of these incompetent people, I've wasted a month of my time (as I said, I was in a real hurry to get a diagnosis) and hours of stressful and anxiety-inducing tests, and now I have to find another clinic and go through the same thing.

500€ down the drain. You pay an additional 100€ for the tests and the psychiatrist's consultation (25 minutes), and the results tell you that, from the center's (psychologists') point of view, you do have ADHD, but the psychiatrist (the one with the prescribing authority, if needed, and the one who's supposed to be the mental health specialist) says you don't. So what's the verdict? Do I have ADHD or not? And the 100€ for the neurologist? Let's not even talk about it. He makes you walk four steps, asks three absurd and irrelevant questions, and sends you home. A complete rip-off that doesn't help you at all. And then there are the prices of the therapies. It's a totally frustrating experience to have suffered with this for years, wanting a good report from "professionals," only to find out they can't even agree among themselves.

one_star_reviews.text:
A terrible experience. I don't blame the employees, but rather the directives given to them by the owners or managers. I live 50 meters from the pharmacy and I stopped being a customer more than 10 years ago. The reason was that they refused to fill my MUFACE prescriptions because the doctor didn't stamp them. I told them that the prescription states in the box that the doctor has to fill in, only their signature and medical license number. They said that MUFACE wouldn't pay them for the prescriptions that way. I called MUFACE and they said that was a lie, that they only needed a signature and medical license number. I had to change pharmacies, where I've been going for more than 10 years and they've never given me any problems with prescriptions.

Yesterday, while my pharmacy was closed, I went to this one to pick up some medication. The employee told me she couldn't fill them because the color of the pen used for the doctor's signature didn't match the color of the pen used to write the medication. I've been filling out the prescription information myself for over 10 years. It saves the doctor's appointment time, and he thanks me for it. He reviews, signs, and stamps it—yes, he has a stamp. Anyway, the medication wasn't dispensed, so I'll be filing a complaint with Muface (the civil servants' mutual insurance company) and the pharmacists' association. Thanks for reading, and you don't need to reply.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wasn't planning on writing this review, but seeing that it's a recurring issue, I felt I had to speak up so others can be careful. I've shopped at this supermarket several times, basically since it opened. Every time I pay in cash, they give me less change. Sometimes it's 20 cents, and you think, "Oh well, it's 20, no big deal." But sometimes it's more than €1, and it's always like that. There are two possibilities: either their cashiers don't know how to count and give change correctly, or it's a trick the employees or the company itself have up their sleeve. It's unbelievable that not once have I paid in cash received the correct change. And of course, it's 10 cents, 30 cents, €1 per customer—that's how they make a killing! It seems trivial, but it's not. It's very serious. I recommend that all customers, no matter how rushed they are, carefully check their change. Furthermore, this is the only supermarket where this has happened to me, and it's always with different cashiers. It's not just one who does it; it's ALL of them.

OH BE CAREFUL PEOPLE.

one_star_reviews.text:
A rather peculiar experience.

I was particularly struck by how easily certain functions related to physical exercise and nutrition seem to be carried out without it being entirely clear what the qualifications or university training of each professional are.

And when we're talking about training people with medical conditions, one would expect training to be a minor detail… although it seems they've taken the "learning on the job" approach quite seriously here. 😅

Perhaps it would be helpful if the center clearly indicated the qualifications and skills of each team member. Transparency in these matters is always beneficial; after all, you don't need to raise the bar for professional qualifications just to train with weights.

A constructive critique: more clarity about who does what and with what qualifications would be appreciated.

The information/security staff don't offer any more information than to call at 7:30 in the morning or go to the door at 9:00 because there are only 30 numbers (a meager 30 numbers), and if you're selected, you'll get a spot that day. If not, you might end up in Requena, Extramurs, or possibly even Madrid. If you're selected, you're selected, because luck is fickle.

one_star_reviews.text: Came two times and still closed. I follwed the timing on his shop as below.. Still the guy is missing.. Worst.

I am completely outraged by the actions of this veterinary clinic and feel it necessary to explain what happened.

After my mother passed away, they gave her dog to someone else, claiming that my mother had no family. Well, it turns out she did have family. And wouldn't you know it, here I am. Furthermore, I am the heir named in her will.

What I don't understand is how they can give an animal to another person and change ownership based on the fact that a deceased person "had no family," without first checking if there were relatives, heirs, or documentation proving who should be responsible for her animals.

And the most infuriating part comes next.

When I found out what had happened, I complained, provided documentation, and explained the situation, hoping the veterinarian would do something to try to resolve the problem. The response? Nothing.

They didn't block the microchip while the situation was being clarified, I have no evidence that they notified the relevant authorities, and they don't seem to have any intention of investigating.

And there's another issue that I find extremely serious: they haven't even checked if my mother had any other animals registered in her name. Because if she did, what's happening to them? Who's verifying who's listed as the owner? Who knows where they are? Who's looking after them?

Is there really no verification of anything before handing over an animal and changing its ownership?

We're talking about the animals of a deceased person. We're not talking about objects that can be given to just anyone because someone says they had no family.

I have documentation proving my status as an heir, and yet I have to fight to get someone to simply review what happened and help me get my mother's animals back.

The feeling I'm left with is that they've taken my dog ​​away, and nobody wants to take any responsibility for how it happened.

And what infuriates me the most is that, after filing a complaint, there doesn't even seem to be any willingness to protect the animal while it's clarified who actually has the right to it.

As a veterinarian, I believe they should have acted with much greater diligence, checked the documentation, and, given a claim of this magnitude, taken steps to prevent the animal from changing hands while the situation was being investigated.

How can no one check anything? How can they assume that a deceased person has no family without verifying it?

Well, she did have family. And she has an heir.

And meanwhile, I continue trying to recover my mother's animals and hoping someone will take what happened seriously.

The most frustrating thing is that, after I filed a complaint, instead of trying to help me, they even refuse to take action that RAIA itself has indicated the veterinarian should handle.

To me, this demonstrates an absolutely incomprehensible lack of diligence and interest.

one_star_reviews.text:
A regrettable experience that I hope I never have to repeat.

Taking my dog ​​here was, without a doubt, one of the worst decisions I've ever made. During the procedure, a piece of his skin was cut, and when I asked for an explanation, the stories kept changing: first, that the dog was in pain; then, that if it was stitched up, a drain would have to be inserted; and finally, they even denied that he had been cut at all. Luckily, the photographs document what happened.

But the situation didn't end there. When I expressed my doubts and said I was going to request a second opinion from his regular veterinarian, the attitude was, in my opinion, completely unacceptable, and I even felt disrespected as his owner.

I was given a syringe with a cream whose contents weren't properly explained to me, and only four antibiotic pills, with the assurance that it was enough.

It wasn't.

For the next 15 days, I had to take my dog ​​to his regular veterinarian almost every other day to have the area cleaned and all the dead skin removed. Afterwards, more treatments were needed, including Blastoestimulina patches and, in addition, 10 more days of antibiotics, with the corresponding financial cost.

All of this hasn't just cost money. It has meant pain, treatments, medication, travel, and, above all, watching my dog ​​go through a process that I believe could have been avoided.

The facts are documented, and a complaint has already been filed. Now it will be up to the competent authorities to determine the corresponding responsibilities.

I don't expect anyone to agree with me just because. I only hope that what happened is investigated and that, if it is proven that there was professional misconduct, the consequences are faced.

When you work with animals, you're not working with objects. You're dealing with living beings who depend completely on you. For me, that demands professionalism, responsibility, and, above all, respect for them.

one_star_reviews.text:
This was by far the worst experience we’ve had eating somewhere on the island.

1. The menu was extremely dirty. I went around four different tables trying to find a menu that was at least reasonably clean and not disgusting to touch. However, at every table, the menus were incredibly sticky, dirty, and unpleasant to handle.
2. We ordered Bolognese pasta and lasagna. I honestly don’t understand what recipe they used, but the dishes tasted more like tomato paste with a little bit of store-bought pasta than actual meals. The lasagna had absolutely no pasta sheets between the layers. As you can imagine, eating hot tomato sauce with a small amount of minced meat was not exactly enjoyable.
3. The mixed salad was simply chopped vegetables and cabbage. We were not given any oil or other dressing. I have no idea where serving a salad like this is considered acceptable.
4. The mojito — if you sell a mojito as a cocktail, you should warn customers that you don’t actually prepare it like a proper cocktail. We were served a glass with lime and mint added for decoration, along with mojito syrup, sweetened water, a small amount of rum, and ice. Of course, there was no sugar. As you can imagine, it was extremely sweet and not tasty at all. And the price was actually higher than in places where mojitos are prepared professionally.

I absolutely do not recommend this café to anyone. Terrible presentation, terrible taste, and overall a very disappointing experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Well, I'm going to share this review because what happened to my father shouldn't happen to anyone, least of all the elderly. We took my father to this nursing home a little over a month ago. At first, everything seemed fine. They told us they had protocols for certain things. We visited my father very often. He walked in, but every day that passed, we noticed he was getting weaker and losing his will to do anything. In the last few weeks, we had to take him out in a wheelchair. The social worker and the director kept telling us it was due to Alzheimer's and not to worry, that he was well cared for. They repeated that phrase to my mother over and over. Well, my father stopped eating and drinking. The day before, we spoke with the doctor, but he did nothing. The next day, a substitute doctor came and called my brother, telling him she was going to call an ambulance for my father. He arrived at the hospital dehydrated and in very bad shape. He was there for ten days until they recovered him. My father is still alive, but of course... He will never return to this residence. He left this review so that our elders are our treasure and we must take care of them, and when we put them in a residence it is because we have no other choice. I never thought my father would be treated like this.

Overpriced

Personally, I WOULD NEVER RETURN UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. If you're thinking of getting your lashes done here, my recommendation is clear: CONSIDER ALL OTHER OPTIONS BEFORE CHOOSING THIS PLACE.

Disappointing Experience – Long Waits, Wrong Orders, and Overcharging
Visited this evening with friends and unfortunately had a very poor experience. We waited over an hour for food, with one order arriving first and being eaten while the rest of us waited. When the main orders finally arrived, they were incorrect—ribs were served instead of the pork chops we ordered (€25 pp instead of €15 pp) x 2 portions. By that point, my friends were starving, so we accepted the wrong meals
My own main course never arrived. When I asked for the bill after an hour, they tried to hand me my uneaten order in a takeaway box along with the bill. We were also charged adult prices for a child’s plain pasta (charged as spaghetti bolognese when what was requested was a child bowl of plain pasta), and a 10% tip was added automatically without our consent. I only noticed the tip while reviewing the bill afterwards.
Overall, the service was slow, the orders were inaccurate, and I was overcharged by €30+ excluding thd child’s plain pasta which I paid  €13 for. Despite spending a bill of almost €140 I got no food!
I would not recommend this restaurant and will not be returning.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'd like to know what happened to the last bus on line 2 yesterday, Saturday. People leaving work, the nursing home, or anywhere else, were waiting at the bus stops, just like those who finish work late, and without warning, the bus didn't show up. If it broke down, they should have sent another one instead of leaving people tired and stranded. We ended up walking home at noon, and it's not the first time. It's a disgrace, and then they tell you to use public transport!
Another point: I think it's great that they're adding a QR code for people who want to check things, but given the information panels that were there, which were a great help to older people and many others, why are they removing them? I personally want to see on the screen how long it will take, if it's arriving, or not. I don't know who's responsible, the bus company or the mayor, but think about how useful it is for older people to be able to check those screens. Most of them don't even have phones that can scan QR codes.
One last point: we all know who the most frequent users of line 2 are, even though they aren't workers. Oh neighbors, that line is completely unsanitary, a breeding ground for who knows what, you can't even go up there without gagging at times. Analyze the situation and try to find a solution or install ventilation systems that expel those vomit-inducing and unsanitary smells.

After my father died in the hospital in Granada, this funeral home showed up with a coffin inappropriate for a loved one, without giving my two brothers the option to choose the coffin they would have preferred from those suitable for cremation. Now my father's insurance company, after having paid for more than 36 years, is saying, "Yes, indeed!" That a certain Paco gave them both a choice of coffin (LIE). At no point did he offer them a choice; he simply put in whatever coffin they felt like giving him—stained, torn, it looked like it was made of cardboard, very flimsy, awful!!... He didn't deserve that. Now this isn't over, and they have the nerve to say they gave us a choice of coffin!!!!! Another LIE! Stop playing with people's feelings, especially in moments of grief. You operate through deception and distort reality for your own benefit!!!!!

They're despicable, con artists, and have no scruples. They take advantage of the situation and the grief of the families to deceive you, saying they give you the option to choose the casket, which is a complete lie, at least in my case, right Paco? This isn't going to end here, you'll see. They gave us a poor-quality casket, scratched and stained, it looked like cardboard. They're con artists, they think we're idiots, they have no shame whatsoever. WE'LL SEE YOU AGAIN.

A bunch of shameless, unscrupulous swindlers. They arrived at the hospital with a cheap, flimsy, dirty, and broken coffin. They didn't give us a choice, and after we filed a complaint, they told Ocaso that they did give me the option. Here I am, Mr. Paco, tell me to my face that you gave me a choice of coffin and that you didn't just put in the one you felt like giving me. What a bunch of crooks! The difference in price between the coffin you gave us and the one we were entitled to is over €1,000, not to mention the emotional distress. We'll see you face to face because the lawsuit is going ahead. BEWARE OF THIS FUNERAL HOME. SCAM

We go every year, the food is good, but the prices keep going up, and then you end up ordering a single dish and it's not as good. Today they had a dish off the menu that they told us cost €80… Another time they told us that one dish (meat) would be enough for three people… one person ate and was still hungry, it doesn't say. And now, on top of that, the price of the dish is €18-20… We would have ordered more so we wouldn't leave hungry, but those dishes aren't worth those prices.
Then, on top of that, they list bread portions for €2. We ordered two portions of bread and asked, "How much bread comes in a portion?" They replied, "About six pieces per portion." Well, when it came time to pay, they charged us for six portions… €12! €2 for half a slice of bread…?!? I told them, and they said that's how they calculate it, but they'd take it off and only charge for two portions. Okay, fine, that makes sense, but it's not fun having to say things like that anymore. At those prices, they would have to offer double the quantity, or else lower the prices because it's highway robbery.

one_star_reviews.text:
My Extremely Disappointing Experience with Dr. Santiago Elvira and Clínica Egos

From the first consultation, I made it clear that I wanted liposculpture with body contouring and definition. That's what I understood I was contracting and paying for. However, after the procedure, I still have a considerable amount of fat in the areas I expected to be treated, and the contouring I requested didn't turn out as I expected.

Furthermore, the doctor himself introduced me to and recommended the use of additional technologies, including Renuvion, which I also paid for, trusting that I was investing in a more comprehensive procedure and a high-quality result. Unfortunately, the result was the complete opposite of what I expected: a huge disappointment.

What surprised me most was that, later, when I asked about the procedure, the attending physician told me that "liposculpture didn't exist" and that it was a fictitious name, stating that what had been done was only the abdomen and flanks. It was especially frustrating to hear this after having booked and paid for what was presented to me as liposculpture.

When I contacted the clinic to express my dissatisfaction and seek a solution, I also felt treated with indifference and even a degree of derision. The response I received was simply to wait a year.

I understand that surgery needs time to show its final result, but I expected, at the very least, an individualized assessment, transparency, and a more responsible attitude toward my complaints.

I paid for the procedure, for the additional technologies recommended by the doctor himself, and I trusted what was explained to me during the consultation. Unfortunately, my experience was one of profound disappointment.

I am sharing my experience so that others will research carefully, clarify exactly what they are signing up for, and request that everything be put in writing before undergoing any procedure.

The very least I expected was transparency, accountability, and respect as a patient.

one_star_reviews.text:
I hired Cristian to do a partial renovation of my house. Initially, everything was wonderful, and he was very attentive. As mistakes began to surface, problems started to arise.
After tiling the entire bathroom, he installed the shower screen incorrectly, drilling holes in the new tiles where they shouldn't be. He didn't tell me this and tried to cover it up by putting filler in the holes in the wall.
He quoted me €3,000 to smooth and paint the walls of the living room and one bedroom, and the result was disastrous. When I mentioned it to him, his response was, "I think the paint looks fine." Despite sending one of his workers to touch it up, I've attached photos of how the walls look now.
SPC flooring was installed throughout the house, and I had doubts about whether it would look good since it was installed over the existing floor. Cristian assured me there wouldn't be any problem because he would use leveling compound and the floor would be perfect. After two and a half months of living in my house, the floor has started to sink in several areas because it's hollow underneath. Since it wasn't leveled properly and people are walking on it, it's sunk.
One of the electrical outlets installed in the living room came loose from the wall when I unplugged a phone charger, causing sparks and a short circuit that kept tripping the circuit breaker. Since Cristian was away on a trip, I had to call my insurance company, and they told me the wires weren't properly taped, and the outlet wasn't screwed into the wall, just sitting on top. They also mentioned that I was lucky I hadn't plugged in a hairdryer or heater there because it could have caused a fire due to the faulty wiring.
A month and a half ago, I contacted Cristian to come and look at the floor and offer a solution. He hasn't contacted me since. I DO NOT recommend this company for any kind of work. They are not serious about taking responsibility for their mistakes, leaving the customer high and dry.
Services
Tile work installation, Install flooring, Paint indoors
I came from far away, from Almería, and when I arrived I found them closed, even though they say they close at 4:30. 0 professional

one_star_reviews.text:
I took my computer to Ray Electronic because it stopped working that day.

It wouldn't turn on properly, and messages kept appearing saying the PC hadn't been properly shut down or that BitLocker recovery was in progress.

A very friendly guy helped me and told me the diagnostic would cost €10, which would be deducted if I ended up having it repaired.

That same day, they called me and said the problem was that the motherboard, keyboard, and screen were wet, and that the repair would cost around €280.

I was incredibly surprised because my computer had never gotten wet before, and besides, it's a computer that costs around €500.

I called my trusted computer technician to tell him what they'd said, and he clearly told me not to accept that repair, that it didn't make sense, and that I shouldn't even think about leaving it there.

I went to pick up the computer and told the second guy who helped me.

Their reaction was to become quite defensive and tell me they weren't deceiving me.

I even apologized for how I phrased it, but they continued to be quite rude to me.

Finally, I took the computer to another place for a second opinion.

There, they told me it simply needed a motherboard cleaning. They charged me €35, and the computer has worked perfectly ever since.

There was no need to replace the motherboard, keyboard, or screen.

In the end, the diagnosis I received from Ray Electronic turned out to be incorrect, and getting a second opinion saved me €245.

I find this particularly serious because, if I had trusted that first diagnosis and accepted the repair, I would have paid €280 for something I ultimately didn't need.

My experience has been very negative, both because of the diagnosis and the way I was treated when I questioned it. I don't recommend this establishment and advise always getting a second opinion before agreeing to an expensive repair.

one_star_reviews.text:
They don't deserve even one star.
According to their tracking system, a package was delivered on Friday at 6:14 PM to a pickup point. On Monday morning (three days after the weekend), I went to pick it up at the location I requested, and there was nothing there for me. I checked the tracking system again, and it showed that it was delivered on Sunday at 11:00 PM (yes, at night). I complained, and they told me it was delivered by hand on Friday at 3:33 PM! And they gave me the ID number of the person who supposedly received it.
I responded and asked them the following questions: How is it possible to hand-deliver it to someone with an ID card if I requested a pickup point? How can you hand-deliver it to someone before it even arrives at the pickup point?
It's utter nonsense and an unacceptable lack of professionalism.

To all this, they reply that the most important thing is that the delivery driver realized he delivered it to the wrong house and that he's going to fix it. Seriously, they have the nerve to respond like that? If I hadn't sent them three emails, nobody would have known what happened.

And I'm still wondering, how can they confuse a pickup point with a home address? Besides, there's no house or address nearby at that pickup point!

I asked them one last time when and where I'll receive my order, and they completely ignored me. I hope they take action, because this whole thing smells fishy.

one_star_reviews.text:
A deeply disappointing experience

Before ordering, we specifically and unambiguously asked the server whether the Spanish omelette was fresh and homemade. He confidently confirmed that it was. We relied on that representation when placing our order.

What was subsequently served appeared to be a pre-prepared/frozen omelette, simply portioned into a small slice, which was entirely at odds with our reasonable expectation of a freshly prepared dish.

When we raised the matter, the server stated that the omelette had been prepared “last night or perhaps this morning” and then acknowledged that preparing a fresh omelette for every order was not possible.

That is a perfectly legitimate operational choice for a restaurant. What is not legitimate from a customer’s perspective is failing to disclose it before the order is placed. Had we been told that the omelette was prepared in advance, we could have made an informed decision about whether to order it.

Unfortunately, the situation was compounded by the server’s dismissive, discourteous and unprofessional manner. We were told that even if we did not want the dish, we would still be required to pay for it.

We paid the bill in full and did not create a confrontation. This was never about the cost; it was about transparency, accuracy and the fundamental principle of treating customers with respect.

A restaurant is entirely entitled to determine how and when it prepares its food. Equally, a customer is entitled to receive accurate information before paying for that food.

Mistakes or disagreements about food can happen. What is far more concerning is giving a customer a confident assurance about freshness, providing something that appears inconsistent with that assurance, and then responding discourteously when the discrepancy is questioned.

I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and reviews both its standards of customer communication and the way legitimate customer concerns are handled.

Overall, a disappointing experience that could have been avoided through straightforward communication and professional customer service.

one_star_reviews.text: I bought a range hood, cooktop, oven, microwave, refrigerator, and dishwasher from PANDO Catalonia, and their after-sales service is a disaster! The refrigerator is making ice and no one is coming to fix it. The microwave light bulb melts when I turn on the oven, and the glass trays break. I will never buy anything from this brand again. The ceiling-mounted range hood keeps losing its programming and there's no way to get it to connect to the cooktop. Look at other, cheaper brands because it's really not worth the price. I've attached photos of the refrigerator and the microwave light bulb.

Our experience with the Pando showroom has been quite disappointing, especially regarding customer service and the ability to schedule a visit. Since the end of August, we have been sending requests to the showroom's contact number without receiving a single response. Later, I tried to schedule an appointment by email, but it was canceled, and I have no option to visit for two weeks due to their attendance at trade fairs. What is the point of offering a showroom service if it is impossible to access it and receive the advice they promise? It is unheard of that a company with products of this caliber, where expert advice is essential due to all the customizations they offer, can afford to treat those who will ultimately be making the purchase this way.

I bought a wine cooler, an oven, and a microwave. I've been waiting six weeks for a response to an online inquiry, and I've called several times to follow up. It may be a luxury brand, but the service is certainly unacceptable for this brand.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1/5

My experience with Lumon has been absolutely disappointing.

We made a significant investment in the enclosure of our home and paid 100% of the work upfront in June 2025. According to the agreed terms, the expected completion time was 8-10 weeks, but they didn't start installation until the end of September. However, more than a year later, we still have outstanding work and unresolved problems.

The worst part hasn't just been the delays, but the quality of the workmanship. In our case, the finishes have been very poor: poorly applied seals, water leaks, sloppy finishing touches, and work that looks more like the work of an amateur than a professional company.

The impression we've been left with after watching various technicians work is that there's a lack of truly qualified and specialized personnel. We've had to personally inspect, complain, and point out numerous defects that should have been detected before the work was considered complete.

To top it all off, perhaps the most frustrating aspect is the lack of response. We've sent messages, made calls, and filed complaints countless times, and often we simply don't get a response, or we receive replies without a concrete solution. We have to constantly follow up to get any progress.

After more than a year, we're still dealing with defects, unfinished work, and no clear answer as to when everything will finally be resolved.

When you make a significant financial investment and hire a company like Lumon, you expect quality, excellent workmanship, skilled professionals, and after-sales service that responds when problems arise. Our experience has been the exact opposite: delays, shoddy workmanship, lack of follow-up, and having to constantly chase them down.

I wouldn't recommend Lumon to anyone.

The worst private health insurance company by far. And I've experienced it twice.
For years I paid the maximum premium, and when you need them, they cover nothing. They don't always have specialists available. The service is very precarious and sporadically inadequate. My father needed them after a lifetime of paying into the company, and when he got cancer, they abandoned him.
They referred me to the General Hospital of Catalonia because they didn't have emergency specialists, and when they were going to do the neurology tests, they told me no and to go back to them (the private health insurance company). An inhumane mess.
My review is clear: IF YOU DON'T WANT TO BE CHEATED AND LEFT STRANDED, DON'T JOIN THIS INSURANCE COMPANY.

At the Granollers health insurance clinic, the service is terrible in many departments. In the last one I visited recently, the assistant was completely out of it, chattering away and ignoring the phone, which kept ringing in the waiting room. Even the doctor mentioned it. The doctor was very nice, but the assistant, with her airs of superiority, completely ignored her. The patients in the waiting room questioned her behavior. It's a disgrace. The waiting lists in some departments are shameful, and the restrooms... they could really use a facelift. I'm glad I cancelled my membership, like so many others, because it's not what it used to be. The service is a zero. I'm forced to give it one star, but it doesn't deserve any.

No permite poner mi review completa, español e inglés, pondré solo la versión inglesa

A Very Disappointing Experience in a Great Location
La Botica Indiana in Gijón is undoubtedly in a fantastic location: Plaza Mayor. Precisely because of that, it is even more disappointing to receive such poor service on several occasions.
During my most recent visit, we experienced a situation that, honestly, was the last straw. We waited for quite some time without anyone acknowledging us, not even to let us know that we would have to wait. When we finally tried to get the manager’s attention, his attitude was, in my opinion, completely inappropriate. Instead of offering an explanation or apologising for the wait, the situation became uncomfortable and unpleasant. In the end, he refused to serve us the coffee we had ordered and actually asked us to leave the premises, and as we were leaving, the manager even laughed at us.
What concerns me most is that I do not consider this to have been an isolated incident. I have had similar experiences before, and people I know have also told me about comparable situations. When this kind of behaviour keeps happening, it is difficult to believe that it was simply a case of someone having a bad day.
As someone who lives permanently in Gijón, I find it genuinely embarrassing that an establishment located in such an iconic part of the city would treat its customers this way. I am also concerned about the employees working there, because a manager should be an example of professionalism, courtesy and respect, both towards customers and towards their own team.
I would urge the people responsible for this establishment to seriously look into what is happening. Generic responses to online reviews are of little use if no real action is taken afterwards. Running a business is not just about responding politely on the internet; it is about making sure that what happens inside the premises lives up to the image the business wants to project.
As for me, after this experience, I will not be returning to La Botica Indiana, nor will I recommend it to my friends, family or anyone close to me. It is a real shame, because the location is exceptional and the place could offer so much more.

one_star_reviews.text:
On August 3rd, after much deliberation, I decided to celebrate my son's 4th birthday at a party venue. I thought it would be the best decision.

I'm writing this review based on my personal experience to warn others about what can happen if you entrust such a special occasion to a place like this. Most of the pictures you see online don't reflect the current state of the venue, the inflatables they actually have, or what you're actually allowed to enjoy during the event.
In my case, with 28 children, I spent €720. The package included 3 hours (from 6 pm to 9 pm), inflatables and water games, snacks, cake, the distribution of gifts, and then home. The typical birthday party setup.
The inflatable, which was essential for the children to play on, was simply not there. When I complained, they apologized. With all due respect, an apology for something like this is useless to me because the money was more than well spent, and the services that were promised should be provided.

The images you see when you search for the venue, featuring water games, have nothing to do with how the afternoon actually unfolded. It was structured like this: playing with a sponge on their head, then lining up to slide down a trampoline onto another one that slid along the ground. If you look at the water photos, you'll see small pools where the children play and cool off, and various details like sprinklers and games that weren't used at the event or were no longer available. This is a crucial point if your event is in the summer because the heat is literally unbearable. The afternoon snack was great: sandwiches with chicken nuggets, and they could have seconds without any problem. There was also a mini popsicle for each child. I'm giving that space the only star I'm required to give this review. I requested piñatas, extras, but since they didn't offer them or couldn't provide them, I opted for sweets for an extra €1.50 per child. Unfortunately, they didn't have any either.

The girls had to rush to assemble the bags with handfuls of gummy bears mixed together at the last minute.
That said, the girls were very resourceful and dedicated. It's typical that the worker who's there, the one who's on the front lines and makes the business work, is the one who pays the price for the poor management of those above them. When I expressed my dissatisfaction and all the problems we had, I saw that this was common at events like this. At the same time, this (an afternoon event that lasts three hours), they also run a day camp, meaning the children's belongings are left there while your birthday guests play. On several occasions, they very nervously scolded the children for touching bags that were accessible to anyone (even two-year-olds). The appetizers for the adults, with all due respect, were some of the poorest I've ever seen (considering the price, obviously). Very poor. They were already asking us to leave at 8:45 pm. It started at 6 PM. There was a pool where they prohibited the older children from swimming (they didn't even have the inflatable that was supposed to be there, nor the games shown in the pictures). While it's true I didn't ask to use it, thinking the aforementioned games would be there, I think the least they could have done was allow the children to cool off. But they didn't even do that. Most of them were dry and didn't even need to change their clothes. I would never have celebrated a birthday in August like that.

In short, little involvement, lack of communication, and very little commitment. I've celebrated birthdays in much simpler places for much less that were a thousand times better.
For me, my son's birthday is the most important day of the year, and I'll spend whatever it takes to make sure that what they advertise is at least as good as it looks, but nothing could be further from the truth. Less than 3 hours and more than €700… I still can't believe it. I absolutely do not recommend trusting this place for such a special day, and I'm writing this review hoping it will save someone else from the disappointment we experienced. And when things don't match what was agreed upon, a simple "sorry" doesn't do me much good.

My child is a good swimmer and was wearing the required life jacket. During a jump into the water, he surfaced directly underneath the inflatable structure and had great difficulty getting out from under it.

Please don't assume that wearing a life jacket alone makes the situation completely safe.

Terrible service. I was recommended their services in February to install a heating/cooling unit, and everything seemed fine during the initial estimate until they actually came to install it... The pipes were exposed and uncovered, the electrical connection was direct to a junction box without a circuit breaker, which caused other outlets in the house to trip. In the summer, the unit and drain pipe leaked due to poor connections, which we had to fix ourselves because Javier is too busy maintaining public swimming pools during the summer and doesn't take responsibility for anything. Furthermore, it took two days. They were supposed to arrive at 9 am, but didn't show up until 11 am, and then again between 5 pm and 6 pm when they went for lunch. The next day, they were rushed and very rude, blaming me because the ladder they brought wasn't long enough to hang the compressor (even though it had been seen, measured, and included in the estimate). And all of this was priced at €640 for the installation of an air conditioning unit 3.5 meters long, running through two walls.

Good words but a bungler (Javier), his partner is very nice and hardworking but he's "just following orders".

I've just come from the Sea Library in Heliópolis. The state of the books is shameful; the deterioration is obvious. Old, torn, dirty, worn... It's even repulsive to touch them. Not everything is acceptable, and I don't care anymore if they're titles that are repeated year after year; it's the condition they're in that matters. I don't think the residents and summer visitors deserve this. Books, like everything else, have a lifespan. It's time to remove what's there and replace it with new works, or if not, rotate the books with the town library and the Villa Ana library. I repeat, most of the books in the Heliópolis library should be removed.

In addition to posting this review here, I will write an email to the town hall notifying them of the deplorable condition of these books. I should also mention that this is the first year the Sea Library has closed on Mondays.
